- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.00 sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (especially -1.00) — model often fails to recognize downward momentum early.
- Lag in downward corrections: model delays price drops after negative sentiment, especially if recent prices are high.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean in either direction.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then overcorrects later.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is +1.00, don’t assume price will stay high; if -1.00, don’t assume price will crash — adjust for sentiment decay or reversal signals.
